calls.thesis: First explicit PLTR call (prior 2 Oct entry was a passing mention only, UNCERTAIN). Says he is buying it now: business graded A+ with 157 net dollar retention, 93% revenue growth, 57% cash growth and forward P/E down 76 to 53, yet stock down 11% over 12 months. Short-term spike after earnings needs a triple beat only: beat guidance ($2.164B), beat consensus ($2.18B, $0.41 EPS) and accelerate past prior quarter's 93% growth (needs $2.28B); otherwise a 5-15% dip is likely, but long-term holders should focus on fundamentals, not the print, and not buy/sell into earnings.
calls.price_at_call: Bear $495 (now his floor), base $717, bull $978, headline target $1,000 (~431% upside)
calls.base_case: Declining growth (95/90/85/80%), 42% net margin, 45x P/E gives $717.
calls.bull_case: Same growth pattern, 46% net margin, 55x P/E in 2030 gives $978, rounded to $1,000 target.
calls.bear_case: Bear case is now $495 on declining growth, 38% net margin, 35x P/E (~170% upside); risks flagged are client concentration, >85% US revenue with little European presence, and 13.7% of revenue to stock-based compensation.

calls.thesis: Palantir could be one of the biggest winners from turning AI into real-world business decisions (revenue expected up 83% this year, ~50% next year; $3.4B operating/free cash flow, $2B+ cash), but valuation is the big risk at 163x earnings / 80x sales — he wants it down to around $160 or even $150 a share before jumping in too much and is not loading up at the current price.
calls.price_at_call: His buy zone $150-$160; analyst average target $212 (~13% upside), low target $80 (-57%) as stated
